title: Oyster Mushroom Asada
cScaleSummary: Oyster mushrooms, coffee, tomato paste, and spices create deep flavor with essentially no dietary cholesterol and very little saturated fat.
ldlActiveSummary: While highly cholesterol-conscious, this recipe does not contain a significant source of legumes, whole grains, nuts, seeds, or other strongly LDL-supportive ingredients.
intro: This mushroom-based take on carne asada uses coffee, tomato paste, Worcestershire sauce, lime, and spices to create a dark, smoky, deeply savory filling with crisp charred edges.

stepGroups.title: Instructions
items: Combine {{ingredient:tomato-paste}}, {{ingredient:black-coffee}}, {{ingredient:worcestershire-sauce}}, {{ingredient:lime-juice}}, {{ingredient:smoked-paprika}}, {{ingredient:ground-cumin}}, {{ingredient:black-pepper}}, {{ingredient:cayenne-pepper}}, {{ingredient:kosher-salt}}, and {{ingredient:olive-oil}} in a small saucepan.
Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer and cook until smooth and fully combined.
Reserve approximately one-third of the marinade for the finishing sauce.
Toss {{ingredient:oyster-mushrooms}} with the remaining marinade and let stand for 5 to 10 minutes.
Simmer the reserved marinade until reduced by about half and slightly syrupy.
Heat a large cast-iron skillet over high heat.
Add {{ingredient:oyster-mushrooms}} to the skillet, leaving excess marinade behind in the bowl.
Cook until the mushrooms release their moisture and the liquid evaporates.
Continue cooking until the mushrooms are deeply browned and charred around the edges.
Transfer the mushrooms to a bowl and toss with the reduced sauce and {{ingredient:cilantro}}.
